title: Nine triggers, one discover: ordering the Gishath cascade so the once-per-turn lands at X=6

board.you: Combat damage step. Gishath, Sun's Avatar (7/6, vigilance, trample, haste) attacked the open seat unblocked and dealt 7. Also on the battlefield: Pantlaza, Sun-Favored (4/4 — its once-per-turn discover has NOT been used this turn), Garruk's Uprising, eight lands (two untapped).

stack.note: Resolving now. Revealed seven: Regisaur Alpha (4/4 Dino), Ripjaw Raptor (4/5 Dino), Carnage Tyrant (7/6 Dino), Ravenous Sailback (3/4 Dino), Cultivate, Mountain, Path to Exile. You put all four Dinosaur creature cards onto the battlefield — one event, simultaneous entry; the three non-Dinosaurs go to the bottom in random order.

extras.context: The simultaneous entry produces NINE triggered abilities you control, all placed on the stack in any order you choose: four Pantlaza discover triggers (X = each enterer's toughness: 4 for Regisaur Alpha, 5 for Ripjaw Raptor, 6 for Carnage Tyrant, 4 for Ravenous Sailback), three Garruk's Uprising draws (Regisaur, Ripjaw, and Carnage Tyrant have power 4+; the 3-power Sailback does not), Regisaur Alpha's create-a-3/3-token trigger, and Ravenous Sailback's modal ETB. Regisaur Alpha's haste grant is a static ability — every Dinosaur you control has haste regardless of what order anything resolves. This is the exact scenario of verified stack 001.
extras.constraint: Pantlaza's rider is once each TURN, not once each combat or once each event — whichever discover you take here is the only one until your next turn.

scenario.question: You choose the order for all nine triggers. Which Pantlaza trigger do you actually take, and where in the stack does Regisaur Alpha's token trigger go?

branches.choice: Carnage Tyrant's discover on top, Regisaur's token trigger on the bottom — take X=6, decline the rest
branches.line: Stack them like a professional. Token trigger first (bottom), then Sailback's modal trigger, then the spare Pantlaza triggers (X=4, X=5, X=4), then the three Uprising draws, and Carnage Tyrant's Pantlaza trigger LAST — last on means first off. Discover 6; decline the spare discovers as they resolve. The token enters dead last, after the once-per-turn is already spent, so its arrival cannot generate a live Pantlaza trigger.
branches.signals: To the table this is one flurry of value. But a pilot who visibly sequences the discover ahead of the token just told everyone they know this deck cold. Expect Pantlaza to move up the removal queue. Wear it as a compliment.
branches.coalition_risk: Nothing beyond what the connection already bought. The table responds to the cascade, not to your bookkeeping.
branches.coaching:
This is verified stack 001's exact line — five new bodies, three draws, and the discover at X=6 off one connection. It's yours for the price of ordering triggers like you mean it. The stack is last-in-first-out and you control all nine placements, so taking less than the maximum X is leaving money on the table.

Discover 6 stops on the first nonland at mana value 6 or less and casts it free, and this deck's density of 5- and 6-drops makes that ceiling worth guarding. It gets better: a free-cast Dinosaur is also a Dinosaur ENTERING, and with Forerunner of the Empire on the battlefield every entry can arm the verified ping web (stack 005). Max-X is engine fuel, not just a body.

Burying the token trigger is the discipline that seals it: it resolves after the discover is spent, so the 3/3 enters triggering nothing. And the haste question is already answered — Regisaur's grant is a static ability, so entering last costs the token nothing. Ceiling secured, zero leaks. That's the play.

citations.quote: First, each player, in APNAP order, puts each triggered ability they control with a trigger condition that isn’t another ability triggering on the stack in any order they choose.
The stack keeps track of the order that spells and/or abilities were added to it. Each time an object is put on the stack, it’s put on top of all objects already there.
An ability triggers only once each time its trigger event occurs. However, it can trigger repeatedly if one event contains multiple occurrences.

branches.choice: Token trigger on top — 'get the body online first'
branches.line: Place Regisaur Alpha's token trigger last so it resolves first, making the 3/3 immediately, then work through the draws and discovers.
branches.signals: Looks proactive — a body online against removal, an extra attacker for a second combat. Both reads are mirages. The token has haste from Regisaur's static ability whenever it enters this turn, and nothing on this stack threatens it.
branches.coalition_risk: None directly. But a cascade that whiffs its discover puts a visibly smaller board on the table, and the wrath math across from you gets easier every time your burst underdelivers.
branches.coaching:
Here's the leak stack 001 exists to teach, and I want you to see it coming from a mile away. The token enters while your four Pantlaza triggers still sit UNRESOLVED beneath it. And because you haven't taken the discover yet this turn, the once-per-turn rider doesn't stop the token from triggering Pantlaza AGAIN — a fifth trigger at X=3 that lands on TOP of the stack and resolves before your X=6.

Now you're threading a needle you strung yourself. Decline the X=3 and every spare perfectly, or say yes one trigger early and burn the once-per-turn at the floor — a discover capped at mana value 3 in a deck whose payoffs start at 5.

And the prize for taking on that risk? Nothing. The haste is static; the body was never in danger. Resolve the discover BEFORE the token trigger, always — great pilots make zero-upside risks simply disappear.

citations.quote: A triggered ability may have an instruction followed by “Do this only once each turn.” This ability triggers only if its source’s controller has not yet taken the indicated action that turn.
Each time an object is put on the stack, it’s put on top of all objects already there.

branches.choice: Take the first spare discover at X=4 — 'a cheaper X digs deeper for cheap spells'
branches.line: Order the triggers casually and say yes to the Regisaur Alpha discover (X=4), reasoning that a lower X skips your expensive cards and digs toward cheap interaction or ramp.
branches.signals: Invisible from across the table — which is exactly why this mistake survives in playgroups for years. Nobody corrects the leak nobody sees.
branches.coalition_risk: None. The bill is paid entirely out of your own expected value.
branches.coaching:
Credit where it's due — the digging logic is real. Discover X skips nonlands above X, so X=4 digs past a 5-drop that X=6 would stop on. But it's optimizing the wrong turn.

You just put five bodies onto the battlefield. You don't need the Cultivate a deep dig finds; you need the biggest free spell in the library. X=6 is the widest net — it stops on everything X=4 stops on, plus everything a 5- or 6-drop IS. On the turn your board quintuples, ceiling beats depth, every time.

Take X=6 off Carnage Tyrant and decline the rest. If what you genuinely need is land, remember discover is a 'may' — declining all four is legal and keeps the library intact. The one play that is never right: spending your once-per-turn at X=4 while an X=6 sits one trigger away on a stack whose order YOU control.

citations.quote: First, each player, in APNAP order, puts each triggered ability they control with a trigger condition that isn’t another ability triggering on the stack in any order they choose.

recommendation.choice: Carnage Tyrant's discover on top, Regisaur's token trigger on the bottom — take X=6, decline the rest
recommendation.rationale:
Verified stack 001 establishes the payoff and the trap in one artifact. Ordered correctly, the cascade yields five bodies, three draws, and a discover at X=6. Ordered token-first, it leaks a fifth Pantlaza trigger at X=3 that sits on top of your best one and dares you to spend the once-per-turn at the floor.

The order is entirely yours (CR 603.3b). The token loses nothing by entering last, because Regisaur's haste grant is static. And X=6 is the widest free-cast net in a deck built out of 5- and 6-drops — with Forerunner of the Empire in the 99, the free-cast Dinosaur's entry is also fuel for the verified ping web (stack 005).

Discover before the token, ceiling over depth, every time. That's how a champion runs nine triggers.
